metadata.title: Anthropic shares jump 34% in Nasdaq debut after record IPO

content.text:
Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) shares surged in their Nasdaq debut on Thursday, opening at $111.50, up 34.3% from the artificial intelligence company's IPO price of $83, giving it a fully diluted market valuation of about $2.02 trillion.
The listing followed a record-breaking $81.34 billion public offering, which attracted demand for nearly seven times the number of shares available.
Including a separate $26 billion private placement involving seven major technology companies, Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) raised a combined $107.34 billion at its IPO price.
The private investment brought in $10 billion each from Google and Nvidia, alongside $2.5 billion from AMD and $1 billion apiece from Broadcom, Micron and Microsoft. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) invested a further $500 million.
The private placement was separate from the public offering, with participating companies receiving non-voting shares.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei marked the listing by ringing the opening bell at Nasdaq, where he highlighted the potential of artificial intelligence to accelerate scientific and medical progress.
"I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade," Amodei said.
He also pledged that the company would remain independent in its decision-making, saying: "We will not bend to either business nor political pressure."
The IPO attracted interest from both retail and institutional investors, although allocations varied significantly.
Retail investors received about 15% of the public offering, while most institutional investors reportedly received no shares as existing backers were prioritised, according to Bloomberg.
Japanese investors secured approximately $3 billion worth of shares, at the lower end of the planned $3 billion to $3.5 billion allocation.
In the UK, more than 100,000 retail investors participated, with nearly two-thirds receiving their full requested allocation.
The strong opening gives public-market investors their first opportunity to gain direct exposure to Anthropic, one of the leading developers of advanced AI models.
The company's market debut will also provide an important test of investor appetite for AI developers as spending on computing infrastructure and increasingly capable models continues to reshape the technology sector.
